channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: Two Iranian Men Charged Over Plot Targeting UK Jewish Community
item.description: Two Iranian nationals who entered the UK on small boats have been charged with preparing acts of terrorism, the Metropolitan Police said in a statement, with tensions between Britain and Iran already high over another security incident.

item.title: From first solo trip at 13, she’s now just 9 countries away from becoming the youngest person to visit every country
item.description: Sophia Lee began travelling alone at 13 with a trip to Costa Rica. Now 20, the American traveller is pursuing a record to become the youngest person to visit every UN-recognised country, with nine destinations left.

item.title: Anant Ambani steps in after family raises ₹2.2 crore for toddler’s ₹9 crore treatment | Watch
item.description: A fundraising campaign for 23-month-old Vedansh Singh, who has SMA Type 1, has received a major boost after influencer Mayuresh Gujar claimed Anant Ambani offered to cover his ₹9 crore treatment cost, with confirmation still awaited.

item.title: Jeff Bezos gives $25 million to protect Pacific Ocean: What the Amazon boss' $10 billion climate pledge aims to achieve
item.description: The latest grants will support projects in the Cook Islands, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and Vanuatu, covering more than 625,000 square miles of ocean.

item.title: On ventilator and unconscious, what's next for Christa Pike after surviving lethal injection
item.description: Pike's attorneys are now seeking commutation of the death sentence, while the state faces an independent review of how an execution that was supposed to end Pike's life instead left her critically ill in a hospital.

item.title: South Africa mass shootings: What’s behind the sudden spike in gun crime? 46 dead in a week in 5 incidents
item.description: South Africa has recorded at least 46 deaths in five mass shootings in less than a week, renewing concerns over organised crime, illegal firearms, and violence in poorer communities despite a recent decline in the national murder rate.

item.title: Hackers Breached Propulsion System of US-Bound Oil Tanker
item.description: FBI and US Coast Guard investigators have found evidence that hackers accessed the propulsion system of an oil supertanker as it was approaching the Texas coast this summer, according to US officials familiar with the matter, an extraordinary breach that highlights the growing physical risks from cyberattacks.

item.title: 'Smallest trader receives...': What Piyush Goyal said as he rejects conditional MFN treatment at G20 meet
item.description: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal made it clear that India opposes linking the Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) status to voluntary or selective WTO rules. He was attending the the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting Session.

item.title: Putin warns Russia will use ‘all weapons’ against NATO aggression: Why Kaliningrad is latest flashpoint
item.description: The latest exchange over Kaliningrad therefore reflects a broader security dilemma: NATO says its military exercises are intended to deter threats and protect its members, while Russia portrays the same activities as preparations for aggression against its territory.

item.title: Tukaram Mundhe in action! Maharashtra FDA cancels Cipla's Pune drug sale licence
item.description: Maharashtra FDA cancels Cipla's Pune drug sale licence over alleged violations in storage, packaging and record-keeping.

item.title: ‘Worked 6.5 days/week, 14 hrs/day’ - No time even for haircut, calling home? Chennai entrepreneur on work-life balance
item.description: A Chennai entrepreneur has revived debate around India’s work culture after claiming he worked up to 14 hours a day and six-and-a-half days a week at a private construction company between 1986 and 1994.

item.title: Pargat Singh appointed Punjab Congress chief ahead of assembly elections after Raja Warring resigns
item.description: Pargat Singh has been appointed Punjab Congress chief ahead of the Assembly elections, replacing Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who resigned from the post. The change comes amid infighting in the state unit.

item.title: Explainer | PepsiCo, Monster challenge order against use of 'Energy Drink' labels but why FSSAI calls them misleading
item.description: PepsiCo and Monster Energy have sued the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India over its directive against the use of ‘energy drink’ in labels. The companies said the restriction would have ‘grave commercial consequences’ and hurt ‘substantial investments’.

item.title: ‘There are no rules now’: Zelensky reveals Putin’s alleged new war order
item.description: According to the Ukrainian president, the alleged change came as Russia intensified its aerial attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, with strikes hitting schools, hospitals, data centres and other infrastructure.

item.title: She gave up her US Green Card to return to India and build her startup from scratch: Meet Bharathi Ramesh
item.description: Nutritionist and entrepreneur Bharathi Ramesh gave up her US Green Card and returned to India after personal loss, health struggles and burnout, choosing to focus on building her startup rather than continue a demanding life in America.

item.title: Piyush Goyal calls for WTO-compliant measures to address global trade distortions at G20 meet
item.description: Piyush Goyal warns against using supply-chain diversification as a pretext for measures that fall outside the multilateral trade framework.

item.title: Why are French students taking to the streets? Around 400 schools shut as protests spread across the country
item.description: Around 400 French high schools have been closed as student protests over teacher shortages, overcrowding and poor facilities spread nationwide, with clashes, fires, and arrests prompting the government to step up security talks.&nbsp;

item.title: Dipke takes 'incompetent' jab at govt as thousands attend CJP's protest at Shivaji Park to seek CEC's resignation
item.description: CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke called the government incompetent as thousands joined the party's Mumbai protest seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

item.title: FlyDubai incident: Israeli plumber says TV show taught him how to stabilise plane; where to watch the show on OTT?
item.description: A documentary saved the FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv from crashing after the alleged fight in the cockpit. A hero passenger was able to pull up the steering control and land the plane safely in Saudi Arabia with help.

item.title: US jobs report September 2026: Hiring slows sharply to 29,000 jobs, unemployment rises to 4.2%
item.description: Hiring dropped from a revised 133,000 in August, Labor Department reported. The unemployment rose to a still-low 4.2% from 4.1% in August

item.title: Brace for price spike: Mumbai toll rates rise for commercial vehicles, transporters warn of freight shock
item.description: The revised charges are applicable at five entry points to Mumbai — Airoli, Mulund LBS, Mulund Eastern Expressway, Dahisar and Vashi.

item.title: Trump weighs diesel export ban; Macron rallies G7 leaders over surging energy prices — inside transatlantic energy clash
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron plans a G7 leaders’ call on surging fuel prices as the US pressures European allies to release emergency diesel stocks. France has urged coordinated action without export curbs, while EU countries weigh releasing additional diesel and crude reserves.

item.title: UAE terms FlyDubai flight incident a ‘terrorist act’, praises pilot Smit Machchhar
item.description: Recently, a FlyDubai flight experienced a mid-air crisis while travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The co-pilot of the flight attacked Indian captain Smit Machchhar in an alleged attempt to crash the flight carrying more than 170 passengers.

item.title: CJP protest in Mumbai: Security arrangements in and around Shivaji Park ahead of Jail Bharo Andolan
item.description: CJP protest is scheduled to take place in Mumbai's Shivaji Park at 4 pm despite police denying permission. Protestors are seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

item.title: India formally names 28 places and features in Ladakh on official map amid China push | Why it matters
item.description: India has formally named and mapped 28 places and geographical features in Ladakh on official Survey of India maps, following a similar exercise in Arunachal Pradesh. The move comes amid China’s practice of assigning Chinese names to locations in Indian territories.

item.title: 'Judge cannot decide this case': Curative plea in SC seeks recall of earlier verdict on CEC, ECs appointment law
item.description: The plea by Jaya Thakur comes in the wake of some claims in media reports that the son of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, who was part of the bench that delivered the split verdict, is the poll panel's standing counsel before the Madhya Pradesh High Court.

item.title: EC orders special drive for left-out, new voters in states where SIR is over amid Gyanesh Kumar-Oppn row
item.description: The instruction was conveyed in writing on September 29 and repeated at a video conference with all state Chief Electoral Officers (CEOs) Thursday, followed a virtual meeting with state CEOs.

item.title: Did you know? Mahatma Gandhi was nominated for Nobel Peace Prize 5 times - Here’s why he never won
item.description: When the Dalai Lama was awarded the Peace Prize in 1989, the chairman of the Nobel Peace Prize committee said that this was ‘in part a tribute to the memory of Mahatma Gandhi.’

item.title: Who's buying BrahMos from India and why? Defence Secretary says exports to cross $600 million
item.description: Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh says BrahMos is a benchmark for India’s emerging export story, with exports to cross $600 million.

item.title: Explained: Why didn't Christa Pike die despite two lethal injections? The first such case in 207 years
item.description: Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee was unsuccessful after she received two doses of pentobarbital. Despite being strapped to a gurney, she remained alive, eventually being hospitalised.&nbsp;

item.title: Pak will continue to acquire technologies: Maj Gen Anand (Retd) on why India needs to maintain tech edge | Exclusive
item.description: Pakistan is likely to sharpen its military capabilities by learning from Operation Sindoor and acquiring technologies with support from China and Turkey, Maj Gen Pawan Anand (Retd) said. He stressed that India must maintain its tech edge through AI, high-compute capabilities and digital engineering.

item.title: ‘I was reciting Hanuman Chalisa’: ‘Hero’ pilot Captain Smit Machchaar recounts flydubai stabbing to PM Modi
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke to Captain Smit Machchaar, who foiled an alleged attempt by his co-pilot to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight, and applauded his bravery.

item.title: SEBI relies on amended rules in Embassy REIT ‘Fit and Proper’ matter, tells Bombay HC no disqualification made out
item.description: SEBI told the Bombay High Court that its examination of complaints concerning the “fit and proper” status of persons associated with Embassy Office Parks REIT was completed after the regulatory framework was amended in April 2026.

item.title: ‘He tried to crash the plane:’ New video shows bloodied Captain Smit Machchhar after chaos on flydubai flight
item.description: In a video shot inside the flydubai plane, one person could be heard saying, “he tried to crash the plane,” in reference to the Omani copilot who stabbed the plane’s Indian captain.

item.title: Section 163 imposed in Delhi: What it means amid protest in Jantar Mantar against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
item.description: Delhi Police has imposed Section 163 across New Delhi ahead of a proposed Jantar Mantar protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today. The order bars gatherings of five or more without permission, demonstrations, slogans and certain items. Security has been tightened amid expectations of a large turnout.
